DECISION GATE (a) RESOLVED — version bump chosen, with a partition rule rather than a migration. Implementation is on branch fix/write-primitives-catalog-v2, worktree BenchBox.wt-write-primitives-catalog-v2, commit 4e8e160ec, published as PR 2342 onto develop.

Rule recorded: results are partitioned by catalog version and the partitions are not comparable. A version-1 bundle compares only to other version-1 bundles and is excluded from version-2 aggregates. Version-1 measurements are never rewritten or transformed, because the underlying SQL differs; re-running the benchmark is the migration path. Version 1 and version 2 measure different work — under version 1 a cloud engine received baseline SQL it often could not execute, so operations that previously errored now run.

Independently verified during takeover: catalog version 1 to 2; benchmark _version "1.0" to "2.0"; 136 operations before and after with none added or removed and exactly 86 modified; 75 of those only gained cloud platform_overrides (snowflake 55, bigquery 53, databricks 64); 11 changed their base write_sql via explicit AS aliases on DML self-references and explicit CAST(... AS NUMERIC) on generated batch values. Those 11 affect every platform, not just cloud, so they were executed against real DuckDB under both catalogs using the benchmark setup path: all 11 pass under both, no regression. 51 DuckDB end-to-end write-primitives integration tests pass under both catalogs.

Three retained migration manifests reference fourteen write-primitives bundles from May 2026 that are no longer in the corpus; if restored they belong to the version-1 partition.
